widget.instructions: Drag corner B or use the slider to change the angles.

steps.text: With a hypotenuse of 1, the opposite side is sin θ and the adjacent side is cos θ.
Pythagoras then says sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, for every angle.
At 30°: sin = ½, cos = √3/2. At 45°: both 1/√2. At 60°: sin = √3/2, cos = ½.
So if you know sin θ for an acute angle, cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ).
Cut an equilateral triangle of side 2 in half: the sides are 1, √3 and 2, with angles 30°, 60°, 90°.
Read the ratios from these sides: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2.

recap.text: Recap: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; sin 30° = ½, sin 45° = 1/√2, sin 60° = √3/2.

accessibility.altText: A right triangle with hypotenuse 1 and its sine and cosine shown.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Use the angle slider and the Mark θ buttons; the description gives every ratio.
